h2: Non-destructive testing courses and NDT training programs: how to compare them
html:
People looking for non-destructive testing courses in the US and Canada meet three kinds of provider with very different models, and the names overlap: a nondestructive testing school, an NDT training program and NDT certification classes can describe the same thing or quite different things. The differences that matter are what you leave with and who certifies you.

Three routes into NDT

  • A nondestructive testing school: a technical or community college programme of one or two academic years that combines several methods with materials, welding and mathematics. It suits someone starting from nothing who wants a broad grounding.
  • Method courses from a training provider: one method and level at a time, in a classroom or online, supplying the formal training hours a written practice requires. This is how most working technicians add a method or move up a level.
  • Employer-led training: the company hires, trains through courses and on-the-job experience, and certifies under its own written practice.

Training is not certification

In the US, finishing a course does not certify you. Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A and CP-189 your employer certifies you, for a method and a level, once you have the training hours, the documented experience hours, passing scores on the general, specific and practical examinations, and a current vision examination. Any NDT technician training or NDT inspector training is therefore one input; experience and the employer's examinations are the others. Central schemes such as ASNT 9712 add an independent examination but still require training and experience first. The pages on NDT Level 1, NDT Level 2 and SNT-TC-1A eligibility set out the hours.

What to ask any provider

  • Which methods and levels, and how many formal training hours each course documents.
  • Who teaches it, and whether an ASNT NDT Level III reviews the content.
  • How the hands-on practical is done, and on what equipment and specimens.
  • What paperwork you leave with for your employer's certification file.
  • Whether the course prepares you for the employer's practical examination, not only the written ones.

Where the Atlantis NDT training program fits

Atlantis NDT runs method courses from Level 1 to Level 3 in UT, RT, MT, PT and VT, among other methods, led by an ASNT NDT Level III. Theory is self-paced online, so you can start in any month, with Level III support; practicals are done in the Practical NDT simulator and at your employer's site. For companies, the same courses make up a corporate NDT training program built around your written practice. Prepare for the written examinations with NDT practice tests, and see online NDT training for how the self-paced format works. To plan a course or a company programme, contact the training team.
